status.place: Place “{name}”: click the target position. Arrow keys rotate by 90°.
status.select: Click or drag to select objects. Shift = add/remove. Ctrl = add. Shift + Ctrl = remove.
status.lasso: Draw a loop around objects. Clockwise = fully inside, counter-clockwise = touching.
status.eraser: Click or drag over edges to delete them. Shift = hide, Ctrl = soften.
status.paint: Material “{material}”: click to paint faces. Alt = sample material, Ctrl = connected faces, Shift = all matching faces.
status.sample: Click a face to pick up its material.
status.lineEnd: Click to set the end point, or type a length. | Arrow keys = lock inference direction on/off. Shift = lock inference.
status.lineStart: Click to set the first end point. | Arrow keys = lock inference direction on/off.
status.freehand: Click and drag to draw a freehand curve.
status.rectangleCorner: Click to set the opposite corner, or type length and width (e.g. 2000; 1500).
status.rectangleStart: Click to set the first corner.
status.rotrect2: Pick the second corner (length and direction).
status.rotrect3: Pick the width and the angle.
status.circleRadius: Pick or type the radius. ({count} segments; “12s” changes the number)
status.polygonRadius: Pick or type the radius. ({count} sides; “12s” changes the number)
status.circleCenter: Pick the centre. Type e.g. “48s” to change the segments.
status.polygonCenter: Pick the centre. Type e.g. “8s” to change the sides.
status.arc2Start: Pick the start point of the arc.
status.arc3Second: Pick a second point on the arc.
status.pushpullDistance: Click to set the distance, or type it. | Snaps to corners, edges and faces. {mode}
status.pushpullPick: Click the face to push or pull. | Double-click = repeat the last distance. {mode}
status.offsetDistance: Move the cursor to set the offset, or type a distance.
status.moveTarget: Click to set the target point, or type a distance. | Ctrl = copy on/off. Arrow keys = lock inference direction.
status.moveTargetCopy: Click to set the target point, or type a distance. (copy) | Ctrl = copy on/off. Arrow keys = lock inference direction.
status.moveStart: Click to set the start point. | Ctrl = copy on/off.
status.rotateCenter: Pick the centre of rotation. Arrow keys align the protractor.
status.rotateStart: Pick the start point of the rotation angle.
status.rotateAngle: Pick or type the rotation angle. Ctrl = copy.
status.scaleDrag: Drag to scale, or type a factor. Ctrl = about the centre, Shift = uniform.
status.followmeProfile: Click the profile face that should follow the selected path.
status.followmePath: First select edges as the path (e.g. double-clicking a face selects its edges), then this tool.
status.tapeEnd: Pick the end point. Ctrl toggles creating guides.
status.tapeStart: Pick the start point (point or edge).
status.tapeStartGuides: Pick the start point (point or edge). Guides are created.
status.dimensionStart: Pick the start point of the dimension or an edge.
status.dimensionPlace: Drag the dimension to its position.
status.textPlace: Pick the position of the text.
status.textAnchor: Pick the point the text should point to.
status.section: Click a face to place a section plane. Arrow keys align it with the axes.
status.orbit: Drag to rotate the view. Shift = pan.
status.zoom: Drag up/down to zoom. Shift = change field of view. Type a field-of-view angle (e.g. 35°).
status.zoomwindow: Drag a rectangle to zoom into that area.
status.lookaround: Drag to look around (the camera turns on the spot).
status.walk: Drag up/down to walk, left/right to turn. Arrow keys work too.
status.poscam: Click to place the camera there at eye height.

components.libraryHint: Library objects are built by a script and then placed at the cursor.

soften.hint: Softens edges between faces of the selection whose angle is smaller than the value set.

outliner.empty: No groups or components in the model.

display.empty: No section planes. Tool “Section plane” in the expanded tool set.
display.rulers: Rulers on the axes (m · cm · mm depending on zoom)

select.desc: Selects entities for other tools and commands.
select.step2: Drag from left to right (window) or right to left (crossing).
select.step3: Double-click: face with edges or open a group. Triple-click: everything connected.

line.desc: Draws edges. Closed edges in one plane form a face automatically.
line.step2: Click the end point or type a length.
line.step3: Keep drawing or press Esc to finish.

rectangle.desc: Draws rectangular faces on the ground or on existing faces.
rectangle.step3: Type e.g. “3m;4m” to set the size (also afterwards).

circle.desc: Draws a circle (a polygon with many segments).
circle.step1: Optional: type the number of segments (e.g. “48”).
circle.step3: Click for the radius or type it.

arc2.desc: Draws an arc through two end points and a bulge.
arc2.step3: Drag the bulge and click (a half circle snaps).

arc.desc: Draws an arc from centre, start point and angle.
arc.step3: Click or type the end angle.

arc3.desc: Draws an arc through three points.
arc3.step2: Click a point on the arc.

pie.desc: Draws a circle sector as a face.

freehand.step1: Press the mouse button and drag.
freehand.step2: Releasing ends the curve; close to the start it closes.

pushpull.desc: Extrudes faces into 3D solids or moves them.
pushpull.step2: Move the mouse and click again or type a distance.
pushpull.step3: Double-clicking another face repeats the last distance.

offset.desc: Creates a parallel copy of the face's edges inwards or outwards.
offset.step2: Move the cursor and click or type the distance.

move.step1: Select entities (or point right at them).
move.step3: Click the target point or type a distance.

rotate.step2: Click the centre of rotation (the protractor aligns with faces).
rotate.step3: Click the start angle, then click or type the rotation angle.
rotate.mod2: Arrow keys: align the protractor with an axis

scale.step3: Drag or type a factor (e.g. “2” or “1;2;1”, also a length “3m”).

tape.step1: Click the start point (or an edge for a parallel guide).
tape.step2: Click the end point – the length is in the “Measurements” box.
tape.step3: Type a new length to scale the model.

protractor.desc: Measures angles and creates angled guides.

dimension.step1: Click the start and end point (or an edge).
dimension.step2: Drag the dimension to its position and click.

text.desc: Creates labels with a leader line.
text.step1: Click an entity (a face shows its area, an edge its length).

section.desc: Cuts the model to show the inside.
section.step1: Point at a face (the plane aligns with it).
section.step3: Switch it on/off in the “Display” panel.

eraser.desc: Deletes edges (and the faces next to them).
eraser.step1: Click edges or drag over them.

paint.desc: Assigns materials to faces, groups and components.
paint.step1: Pick a material in the “Materials” panel.
paint.mod3: Shift: all matching faces in the model

orbit.desc: Rotates the camera around the model.
orbit.step2: The middle mouse button works in every tool.

pan.step2: Shift + middle mouse button in every tool.

zoom.step2: The mouse wheel zooms towards the cursor.

followme.desc: Extrudes a profile along a path (e.g. pipe, cornice, lathe shape).
followme.step1: Select the path edges (double-clicking a face selects its edges).

mesh.noTopFaces: The object has no faces on its top level.
mesh.tooMany: Too many polygons ({count} triangles) – that would slow the browser down.
mesh.cannotSimplify: The object cannot be simplified that much.
mesh.moreKeepTitle: Every triangle becomes four – the shape stays exactly the same
mesh.moreRoundTitle: Every triangle becomes four, corners and curves get smoother
mesh.affectsComponent: Works on the top level of the group/component – and so on all its copies. Undo with Ctrl+Z.
mesh.affectsGroup: Works on the top level of the group/component. Undo with Ctrl+Z.
mesh.selectHint: Select a group, component or drawn circle to change its polygon count. Combine loose geometry with “Make group” first.
mesh.exactHint: The object is rebuilt exactly with the new resolution.
mesh.circleHint: Works while the circle is still flat – set it before Push/Pull.
mesh.noMesh: No mesh found – expected lines like “v 1 2 3” and “f 1 2 3”.
mesh.fewAlready: The object already has very few polygons.

welcome.title: Welcome to {name}
welcome.text: Easy 3D modelling right in the browser – with an AI that runs on your own computer. A few short steps show you the essentials.

draw.title: Draw and pull up
draw.text: Draw a face on the ground and pull it up with Push/Pull – that is how walls, furniture and whole houses are made.

navigate.title: Look around
navigate.text: With the mouse you move freely through your model.
navigate.tip1: Drag the middle mouse button = rotate (orbit)

ai.title: The AI assistant
ai.text: Just describe what you want – “a table with 4 chairs” or “a spider with red eyes” – and the AI builds it. It runs locally, e.g. with Ollama; a wizard helps with the setup.

more.title: Terrain, scripts and import
more.text: Shape mountains and valleys with the terrain tool, build objects by script (s3d.box …) or simply drag files from SketchUp, Blender, 3ds Max & co. into the window.
more.tip1: Tool Terrain – brushes for hills, valleys and textures
more.tip2: Script editor on the right – with API info and examples
more.tip3: SKP · BLEND · FBX · 3DS · DAE · OBJ · STL · glTF …

look.title: Your look
look.text: At the top you switch between light and dark – also just the menus or a night scene. You will find this introduction in the menu at any time.
look.tip1: ☾ / ☀ top left – the arrow next to it has more options

box.title: Box
box.desc: Box from the front left bottom corner. Width = X, depth = Y, height = Z.

cylinder.title: Cylinder
cylinder.desc: Upright cylinder standing on its centre. segments = number of sides (default 24).

cylinderBetween.title: Rod from A to B
cylinderBetween.desc: Cylinder or cone between any two points – ideal for legs, branches, pipes, railings. endRadius = radius at the end (0 = point).

cone.title: Cone
cone.desc: Cone with its tip at the top. With endRadius > 0 a truncated cone (lampshade, bucket, flower pot).

pyramid.title: Pyramid
pyramid.desc: Pyramid with a square (sides 4) or n-sided base. kante = length of a base edge.

prism.title: Prism
prism.desc: Upright prism with a regular n-sided base (default 6 = hexagon).

sphere.title: Sphere
sphere.desc: Sphere around a centre with smoothed edges.

dome.title: Dome (half sphere)
dome.desc: Half sphere with a flat bottom – domes, lamps, igloos.

ellipsoid.title: Ellipsoid
ellipsoid.desc: Stretched sphere with three radii – bodies, heads, cushions, leaves, stones.

tube.title: Tube / ring
tube.desc: Hollow cylinder – pipes, cups, rings, wells.

torus.title: Torus (donut)
torus.desc: Lying ring – tyres, life buoys, donuts, handles.

wedge.title: Wedge / ramp
wedge.desc: Ramp rising along +X to its height – ramps, lean-to roofs, wedges.

stairs.title: Stairs
stairs.desc: Straight stairs along +X. Default: 10 steps, 17.5 cm high, 28 cm deep, 1 m wide.

mesh.title: Mesh from OBJ text
mesh.desc: Triangle mesh from “v x y z” and “f a b c” lines (e.g. LLaMA-Mesh). size = longest side.

rect.title: Rectangle
rect.desc: Rectangular face. ebene 'xy' = lying, 'xz' / 'yz' = standing. Then e.g. .pushpull(höhe).

circle.title: Circle
circle.desc: Circular face. normal = direction the face points to ('z', 'x', 'y' or a vector).

face.title: Face from points
face.desc: Any flat face from at least 3 points that lie in one plane.

polyhedron.title: Faces from a point list
polyhedron.desc: Exact geometry like OpenSCAD's polyhedron: punkte = [[x,y,z], …], flächen = lists of point numbers (from 0), e.g. [0, 1, 2, 3], or { outer: [...], holes: [[...]], material: 'Holz' } for faces with holes. This is also the code “Open as code” produces.

line.title: Line / polyline
line.desc: Edges without thickness. A closed flat polyline forms a face automatically.

arc.title: Arc
arc.desc: Circular arc as edges. Returns the points – handy as a path for followMe.

pushpull.title: Push/Pull
pushpull.desc: Pulls a face into a solid. For lying faces a positive value always goes up.

extrude.title: Extrude
extrude.desc: Like pushpull, but in a fixed direction: 'x', 'y', 'z', '-x', '-y', '-z' or a vector.

offset.title: Offset
offset.desc: Draws an inner outline into the face – for frames, windows, borders.

followMe.title: Follow me
followMe.desc: Sweeps a profile along a path – pipes, cornices, frames, lathe shapes.

faceMaterial.title: Colour a face
faceMaterial.desc: Set the material of the front or back of a single face; reverse() flips the face.

group.title: Group
group.desc: Everything created in the callback is combined into one group.

component.title: Component
component.desc: Reusable definition – build it once, place it as often as you like. Changes affect all copies.

transform.title: Move, rotate, scale
transform.desc: All solid functions return a group that can be changed like this (chainable).

copy.title: Copy & more
copy.desc: Copy with offset; material for the whole group; assign a tag; hide; explode into loose geometry.

useMaterial.title: Use a ready-made material
useMaterial.desc: All materials in the list below work directly by their name – without creating them first.

material.title: Own material
material.desc: Defines a material or changes an existing one. texture = one of the textures below, size = tile size in metres.

materials.title: List materials
materials.desc: Names of the ready-made materials (optionally only one category, e.g. 'Metall') or of the textures.

view.title: View
view.desc: Pick a standard view and zoom to everything (done after the script).

camera.title: Camera
camera.desc: Put the camera at a position and point it at a target.

shadows.title: Shadows & style
shadows.desc: Shadows on/off with time of day; change the display – faceStyle: 'textured' | 'shaded' | 'monochrome' | 'hiddenline' | 'wireframe', xray: true = X-ray.

annot.title: Dimension, text, guide
annot.desc: Dimension line between two points, label with arrow, guide line or guide point.

tag.title: Tags
tag.desc: Create tags (layers), show/hide them and assign groups.

clear.title: Delete everything
clear.desc: Empties the model (or the current group). Like everything in a script it can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

units.title: Lengths & units
units.desc: All numbers are metres. Wherever a length is expected, strings with a unit work too.

points.title: Points & axes
points.desc: Points are arrays. The ground is at z = 0.

random.title: Randomness & loops
random.desc: Plain JavaScript – loops, variables and maths are allowed.

log.title: Output
log.desc: Writes to the console below the editor. s3d.stats() returns the number of faces/edges.

apiReference.insertTitle: Insert the example at the cursor

apiReference.tryMaterial: Build a cube with this material

api.zoomExtents: Zoom to everything after the script.

group.rotate: Rotate about an axis ('x', 'y', 'z' or a vector), by default about the group's origin.
group.tag: Assign a tag (layer) – created when needed.
group.copy: Copy with offset – returns the copy.
group.explode: Explode into loose geometry. Returns the number of parts.
group.name: Name of the group or component.
group.ref: Reference { kind, id } to the instance.

face.pushpull: Pull into a solid. For lying faces positive always goes up.
face.extrude: Like pushpull, but in a fixed direction: 'x', 'y', 'z', '-x', '-y', '-z' or a vector.
face.offset: Draw an inner outline into the face.
face.followMe: Sweep a profile along a path.
face.ref: Reference { kind, id } to the face.

component.place: Place a copy of the component.

completion.console: Writes to the console below the editor.

options.material: Material name – ready-made materials work directly by their name.
options.name: Name of the group.
options.group: false = loose geometry instead of a group.
options.sides: Number of sides of the base.
options.normal: Direction the face points to ('x', 'y', 'z' or a vector).
options.smooth: Edges flatter than this angle (degrees) are smoothed.
options.children: List of the objects in the group.
options.faces: Faces as lists of point numbers (from 0).

completion.units: Wherever a length is expected, strings with a unit work.
completion.s3d: The Shap3D.ai script API – solids, faces, groups, materials, view.

scriptEditor.convertTitle: Translate the code into another format – the model stays unchanged
scriptEditor.undoConvertTitle: Bring back the code from before the conversion
scriptEditor.newTitle: Empty script in the chosen language – Ctrl+Z brings the previous code back
scriptEditor.yUpTitle: OBJ files and LLaMA-Mesh are Y-up – turned to Z-up
scriptEditor.smoothTitle: Edges between faces flatter than this angle are smoothed (0 = all edges visible)
scriptEditor.consoleHint: Output of s3d.log(…) and errors appear here. Every run is a single undo step.
scriptEditor.objHelp:
OBJ mesh: lines “v x y z” (vertex) and “f a b c …” (face, vertex numbers from 1).
Everything else (text, # comments, vn/vt, groups) is ignored – raw LLaMA-Mesh output
can be pasted directly. The mesh is scaled to “Size” (longest side),
put on the ground and placed as a component next to the model.
In a JS script: s3d.mesh(objText, { at: [x, y, z], size: '80cm', yUp: true, material: 'Holz' })
scriptEditor.converted: Converted to {format} – the model is unchanged. “Run” builds it in.
scriptEditor.placeholder:
New script, e.g.
{start}

Ctrl+Space shows suggestions, “Load example…” ready-made scripts.
Run with Ctrl+Enter.
scriptEditor.newHint: New script – Ctrl+Z in the editor brings the previous code back.
scriptEditor.objDetected: OBJ mesh detected – language set to “OBJ mesh”
scriptEditor.done: Done – {count} face in the model. | Done – {count} faces in the model.

house.name: House with gable roof
house.description: Box + roof prism, door and windows as groups.

stairs.name: Stairs (loop)
stairs.description: Steps with a for loop, sizes as variables.

spiral.name: Spiral staircase (rotate)
spiral.description: Define a component once, then place it rotated.

fence.name: Fence (row of components)
fence.description: Posts & slats as components – changes affect all copies.

city.name: Random city
city.description: Grid of high-rises with random height and colour.

lathe.name: Vase (follow me)
lathe.description: Turn a profile along a circle – like “Follow me”.

json-shelf.name: JSON: shelf (array)
json-shelf.description: “array” repeats an object with an offset.

mesh-js.name: Mesh in a script (s3d.mesh)
mesh-js.description: Embed OBJ text right in the script, scale it and place it several times.

obj-chair.name: OBJ: chair (LLaMA-Mesh)
obj-chair.description: Raw LLaMA-Mesh output – only v/f lines. Set size and axes above.
